K2SymbolsBrauer.summary: Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti contains any algebraic K-theory: there is no K₀, K₁ or K₂ of a ring, no Steinberg group of a ring, no Milnor K-theory, no tame symbol, no Hilbert symbol and no Weil reciprocity, so every layer of this roadmap is not built. What the libraries do supply is the arithmetic substrate the roadmap runs on, and quite a lot of it: elementary matrices as `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.transvection` and `Matrix.TransvectionStruct`; group homology with `groupHomology.H2`; discrete valuations, uniformisers and residue fields (`IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation`, `Valuation.IsUniformizer`, `IsLocalRing.ResidueField`); Tau Ceti's function-field places with `Place.normResidue` — the exact 'unit part, then residue' discipline T.3 demands — together with `Divisor.eval`, `Divisor.principal`, the product formula `Divisor.degree_principal` and the classification `Place.ratFuncEquiv` of the places of k(t) including ∞; the S-integer class group and S-unit finiteness results; and Tau Ceti's Kummer class map `Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ → H¹(G_K, μₙ)`. Genuinely missing is everything K-theoretic: the Steinberg group and its universal central extension, the symbol and Matsumoto's theorem, the tame symbol and the localisation sequence, Weil reciprocity in symbol form, the tame kernel and the calculations K₂(ℤ) ≅ ℤ/2 and K₂(F_q) = 0, Dennis–Stein symbols, and the Galois-symbol/Hilbert-symbol comparison — the last also blocked by the absence of a cup product on group cohomology and of étale cohomology of schemes.

K3BlochGroups.summary: This roadmap is entirely unbuilt: `grep -rn -i` over both trees finds no Bloch group, no pre-Bloch group, no five-term relation, no Suslin sequence, no dilogarithm, no cross-ratio and no K₃ of anything — and the stable Steinberg group the homological model is built on does not exist either. The genuinely useful infrastructure the libraries already provide is Mathlib's group homology: `groupHomology` in all degrees, computed by the inhomogeneous (bar) complex, with explicit low-degree chain identifications (`groupHomology.chainsIso₃`) and functorial chain maps, which is exactly the chain-level apparatus V.1 and V.6 ask for; plus `CategoryTheory.Tor` for the Tor₁(μ,μ) term, `rootsOfUnity`, tensor products of ℤ-modules, and the number-field invariants r₁ and r₂ (`NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsReal`, `NumberField.Units.rank`) that V.2's arithmetic statement is phrased in. Everything else — the Bloch-group conventions, Suslin's theorem, the configuration complex, and every calculation from K₃(F_q) ≅ ℤ/(q²−1) to K₃(ℚ(i)) ≅ ℤ ⊕ ℤ/24 — is missing. Note the roadmap's own warning is correct: Tau Ceti's many `Steinberg` declarations are Lie-theoretic Frobenius twists and are not this Steinberg group.

KTheoryLowDegrees.summary: This roadmap is the one in the batch with real library coverage, and two clusters of it are effectively already done. On the K₀ side, Mathlib supplies Z.1's projective-module presentation (`Module.Projective.iff_split`, `LinearMap.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective`), essentially all of Z.2 (`Module.rankAtStalk` as a locally constant function on Spec, with base change, localisation and product formulas, plus `Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing` for freeness over a local ring), the Picard group `CommRing.Pic` with `ClassGroup.equivPic : ClassGroup R ≃* Pic R` for Z.4's Pic/class-group comparison, and Morita equivalence; Tau Ceti supplies Z.4's S-integer specialisation outright (`IsDedekindDomain.integerClassGroupEquiv : Cl(𝒪_S) ≃* Cl(R)/⟨[v] : v ∈ S⟩`) and, for Z.5, the elliptic-curve equivalence `Point.toClassEquiv` with `toClass_surjective` — Mathlib has only injectivity — together with an additive, injective divisor-class-to-line-bundle-class map on regular noetherian curves. On the K₁ side, Tau Ceti's `SpecialLinearGroup/Transvection.lean` and `Diagonal.lean` prove, sorry-free and over an arbitrary commutative ring where possible, U.1's type-A commutator relations (`commutatorElement_transvection`: ⁅x_ij(c), x_jl(d)⁆ = x_il(cd)) and Whitehead's identity (`diag2nUnit_decompose`: diag(a, a⁻¹) is six transvections), and U.3's elementary reduction over a field (`closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top_of_field`: SL_n(K) = E_n(K)) and its integral analogue for SL_n(ℤ); for U.4, Mathlib's Dirichlet unit theorem and Tau Ceti's finite generation of the S-units cover everything except the rank formula r₁+r₂+|S|−1. What is genuinely missing is the K-theory itself: there is no K₀ or K₁ of a ring or a scheme, no stable GL(A) or E(A), no determinant/SK₁ decomposition, no Dieudonné determinant, no Bass–Milnor–Serre theorem, no relative K₁ or congruence subgroups for a general pair (A,I), no λ-ring or Adams operations, no Steinitz classification and no I ⊕ J ≅ A ⊕ IJ, no K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X) and no projective-bundle formula. The roadmap documents treat several of the items above as to-be-built that are in fact already proved; those are flagged target by target.

targets.note: `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup` exists for each finite index type, and Mathlib has filtered colimits of modules (`AddCommGroup.DirectLimit`), but the colimit of the GL_n tower — and the stabilisation embedding itself — is not built in either library.

targets.target: Equivalence between finitely generated projective modules and direct summands of finite free modules, with the complement and splitting maps available
targets.note: `Module.Projective.iff_split` is exactly 'projective iff a direct summand of a free module', with the maps i and s produced, and `LinearMap.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective` splits any surjection onto a projective. Finiteness is carried by `Module.Finite`; this target is built.

targets.target: Idempotent matrix attached to a finitely generated projective, and the correspondence between idempotent matrices up to stabilised equivalence and projective isomorphism classes
targets.note: Mathlib has the correspondence between idempotent endomorphisms and complemented submodules (`Submodule.isIdempotentElemEquiv`), but nothing that presents a finitely generated projective by an idempotent matrix, and no stabilised-equivalence classification.

targets.target: Ring K₀ via the existing split/exact K₀ universal property
targets.note: There is no K₀ of a ring or of an exact category in either library. The only Grothendieck group is `Algebra.GrothendieckGroup`, the group completion of a commutative monoid (localisation at the top submonoid) — the correct raw material, but not applied to isomorphism classes of projectives.

targets.target: Object-class induction, equality of classes by stable isomorphism, scalar extension
targets.note: Absent with K₀.

targets.target: Morita functoriality of K₀
targets.note: Mathlib has `MoritaEquivalence`/`IsMoritaEquivalent` and proves R and Mₙ(R) are Morita equivalent; K₀ and hence its Morita invariance are absent.

targets.target: Every short exact sequence of projectives with projective quotient splits (so direct-sum relations suffice)
targets.note: `LinearMap.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective` for a projective quotient is precisely this splitting; it is stated for an arbitrary surjection onto a projective module, more general than the projective-terms case asked for.

targets.target: Rank of a finitely generated projective over a commutative ring as a locally constant ℤ-valued function on Spec A
targets.note: `Module.rankAtStalk M : PrimeSpectrum R → ℕ` with `Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk` (for a finitely presented flat module) is exactly this, and a finitely generated projective is finitely presented and flat (`Module.Flat.of_projective`). Built.

targets.target: Finite image of the rank function and compatibility with localisation and base change
targets.note: `Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange`, `Module.freeLocus_localization` and `Module.rankAtStalk_tensorProduct` supply localisation and base-change compatibility; local constancy on a quasi-compact Spec gives the finite image.

targets.target: On a connected spectrum the rank is a single integer; on a disconnected spectrum it must not be collapsed
targets.note: Mathlib's rank is a function on Spec throughout, so the distinction is structurally respected, and `Module.rankAtStalk_prod` computes it on a product ring; the explicit 'locally constant on a connected space is constant' specialisation for `rankAtStalk` is not stated (though `IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace` is available generically).

targets.target: K₀(F) ≅ ℤ for fields and division rings, by dimension
targets.note: Absent with K₀; `Module.finrank`/`Module.rank` supply the dimension invariant over a division ring.

targets.target: Finite-product formula for K₀ and the test K₀(F × F) ≅ ℤ²
targets.note: Absent with K₀. `Module.rankAtStalk_prod` is the rank-level analogue on a product ring.

targets.target: For local rings, finitely generated projectives are free
targets.note: `Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing` (stacks 00NZ) proves that a finite flat module over a local ring is free; with `Module.Flat.of_projective` this gives the target in greater generality than the layer's Nakayama/finite-presentation route. Built.

targets.target: Semilocal decomposition with the connected-component information
targets.note: Not stated for semilocal rings in either library.

targets.target: K₀ ring structure by tensor product on a commutative ring
targets.note: Absent with K₀; `Module.rankAtStalk_tensorProduct` is the rank-level multiplicativity the ring structure would induce.

targets.target: Exterior powers of finite projectives and the filtration formula for an extension
targets.note: Mathlib has exterior powers ⋀[R]^n M with bases and finiteness, but the development is aimed at free/finite modules; there is no statement that Λⁿ of a finitely generated projective is projective, and no filtration Λⁿ(M) for a short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0.

targets.target: λ-ring identities on K₀ and their extension from modules to virtual classes
targets.note: There is no λ-ring in either library: `grep -i "lambdaring"` is empty and the only mention of λ-rings is a docstring remark in Mathlib/RingTheory/Binomial.lean that binomial rings are the λ-rings with trivial Adams operations.

targets.target: Determinant of a projective of locally constant rank, defined componentwise
targets.note: Both ingredients (rankAtStalk and exterior powers) exist; the componentwise determinant of a projective is not defined.

targets.target: Determinant as an additive-group homomorphism K₀(A) → Pic(A), with tensor product as the Picard operation
targets.note: `CommRing.Pic R` exists as the group of invertible modules under tensor product (`CommRing.Pic.mul_eq_tensor`, `inv_eq_dual`), so the target of the map is fully built; the map itself is absent with K₀.

targets.target: Augmentation/rank kernel and its relation with the γ-filtration; degree-zero normalisation of the Adams operations
targets.note: Absent; no γ-filtration and no Adams operations.

targets.target: Steinitz classification: a positive-rank finite projective over a Dedekind domain is a free summand plus an invertible ideal
targets.note: `grep -rn -i steinitz` over both trees hits only the Steinitz theorem on algebraic extensions (Mathlib/FieldTheory/PrimitiveElement.lean) and Steinitz/supernatural numbers in Tau Ceti. Mathlib's Dedekind-domain module theory (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/DedekindDomain.lean) covers only torsion modules.

targets.note: `ClassGroup.equivPic (R) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] : ClassGroup R ≃* Pic R` is exactly this comparison, for any domain (more general than Dedekind). Built.

targets.note: `IsDedekindDomain.integerClassGroupEquiv : ClassGroup 𝒪_S ≃* ClassGroup R ⧸ ⟨[v] : v ∈ S⟩` is precisely the layer's statement, for an arbitrary Dedekind domain R with the honest localised ring `Set.integer`, together with finiteness of Cl(𝒪_S) and the evaluation lemmas. The class-group half of this target is built; only its K₀ packaging is missing.

targets.note: Mathlib has extension of ideal classes along a ring extension (`ClassGroup.extendedHom`, with composition and evaluation lemmas) and Tau Ceti has the relative-norm map on class groups (`ClassGroup.extendedRelNormHom`) — that is the norm side of the transfer formula at the level of Pic. targets.target: Structure-sheaf and skyscraper-sheaf class formulas through the K/G comparison, so that a divisor class agrees with the line-bundle class
targets.note: The divisor-class/line-bundle-class agreement is half proved in Tau Ceti (injective and additive, surjectivity open), and the function-field product formula `Divisor.degree_principal` fixes the degree. The K-theoretic class formulas need K₀ and G₀.

targets.target: Pic(E) ≅ ℤ ⊕ E(F) for an elliptic curve with origin, hence K₀(E) ≅ ℤ² ⊕ E(F)
